newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea probing president's son trace accounts.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea probing president's son trace accounts.

text.p: State prosecutors investigating South Korean President Kim Young-sam's son in connection with a loans-for-kickbacks scandle on Friday traced accounts of associates suspected of managing funds for him, officials said.

The prosecution had secured evidence that executives of several companies looked after large sums of money linked to Kim Hyun-chul's associates, but the sources of the funds were still being investigated, they said.

A prosecution spokesman could not confirm claims by the main opposition National Congress for New Politics that two associates managed more than 20 billion won ($22 million) of unspent funds from Kim's 1992 presidential campaign.
The president's second son is under investigation over allegations that he meddled in state affairs and kept part of the 1992 election fund.

The younger Kim has also been investigated for his role in a loans-for-kickbacks affair involving failed Hanbo Steel Co, but the spokesman said the prosecution had found no connection between Kim Hyun-chul and the scandal.
"Associates of Mr Kim Hyun-chul will be questioned first before prosecutors seek an arrest warrant against the president's son," said a preosecution offical who asked not to be identified.
He said prosecutors planned to charge Kim Hyun-chul this month with "irregularities unrelated to Hanbo", but gave no other details.

The National Congress has alleged Kim Hyun-chul, who helped engineer his father's 1992 election victory, pressured banks to keep loans rolling into Hanbo Steel in return for a donation worth tens of billions of won to help finance the 1992 campaign.
Kim Hyun-chul has denied any links to Hanbo Steel, which collapsed in January, revealing a web of corrupt alliances between politicians, businessmen and bankers.

National Congress spokesman Chung Dong-young said his party had evidence the country's intelligence chief met Kim Hyun-chul and his associate Kim Ki-sup to discuss a strategy for countering legal steps by the prosecution against the president's son.
"The three met in a luxury hotel in Seoul three days after Kim Hyun-chul testified in parliament on April 25 over the Hanbo case," he said.
The intelligence chief, Kwon Young-hae, admitted meeting them but denied discussing legal counter steps.

The opposition has accused Kim Ki-sup, a former top intelligence officer, of asking the Hansol Group, the nation's 16th-largest industrial conglomerate, to manage seven billion won. Hansol has denied the charge.
"The prosecution plans to summon Mr Kim Ki-sup for questioning soon," the prosecution official said. Kim Ki-sup will be the third associate of Kim Hyun-chul to be investigated by the prosecution.

Two business associates of Kim Hyun-chul -- Park Tae-joong and Kim Hi-chan -- have been arrested on charges that they took bribes in return for promises to lobby the president's son to help them obtain government broadcast licences. (US$1 = 894 won)
